analysis:
The PR changes only docs/reference/ssd-kv-cache.md, a documentation file with no executable change. The substantive additions are head line 125 (new "Same-file coordination" row), line 269 (failure and recency wording), line 377 (TTL row) and line 381 (epoch record read failure row). These document SSDCheckpointFileCoordinator per-file shared/exclusive leases, mtime rewrite throttling to ttlSeconds/30, and a refusal-not-disown policy on transient epoch-record read errors.

Against T-041 and SEC-035:
- The documented TTL is unchanged (defaultTTLSeconds = maxTTLSeconds = 1800) and the docs still cite the sign-off requirement. The at-rest model is unchanged: HMAC-keyed names, AES-GCM and KEK purge.
- The mtime throttle (rewrite only if at least 60 s old) slightly coarsens sliding-TTL recency, within a TTL of 1800 s. This is not a TTL extension.
- A busy corrupt file is documented to stay indexed until a reader finds it alone, a writer validates it, or it expires. This is an availability and cold-miss-only effect, not a confidentiality issue.
- The epoch read-failure policy refuses the operation and keeps the epoch rather than disowning. It does not weaken authentication or purge primitives. It is consistent with the threat model's statement that the epoch is a routing-evidence generation and not an at-rest purge primitive.

No new attack surface, trust-boundary change or invalidated assumption is evident from the docs alone. The implementation (SSDCheckpointFileCoordinator.swift, SSDCacheEpochStore.swift) is not supplied, so the accuracy of these claims and the lease starvation and ordering behavior (T-060-style local DoS by a same-UID process) remain unverified. The next pass should check the code if it is in scope. The patch excerpt is truncated, but the three supplied units cover base and head text.
